subject: Request: GPU price-protection / safety-net clause for Reserved Capacity
messages:
From: Alex Patterson <alex.patterson@clearsight.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@clearsight.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU price protection for reserved commit?

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the detailed sizing walkthrough last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's throughput and the dedicated isolation model. Before we move to redlines, my legal and finance partners have a question about GPU-market volatility. Given the size and 24‑month tenor we're discussing, they want a simple "safety-net" clause so ClearSight isn't locked into a price that becomes materially worse if market GPU spot pricing drops by >25%.

High-level ask: can Redwood include a limited price-protection mechanism tied to a published GPU index or a quarterly review that allows a one-time adjustment (credit or partial rate reset) if market pricing moves >25% over a 90-day period? They're open to guardrails — e.g., eligibility thresholds, minimums, and caps on the adjustment.

Attached is our preferred example language (for context) and a short spreadsheet of scenarios.

Cheers,
Alex

--

What I need:

Subject: Re: Fwd: GPU price protection for reserved commit? — pricing input

Stephanie / team — reviewed the ask and ran the spreadsheet through our pricing model. High level input:

1) Commercial construct we can support (subject to approvals):
   - Single invocation safety‑net tied to a published hardware index (we propose the "Redwood GPU Index" benchmarked to publicly reported spot prices).
   - Trigger: sustained delta >25% (customer benefit) averaged over a 90‑day trailing window.
   - Remedy: customer may elect either (A) a one-time credit equal to 50% of the delta applied to next invoice(s) up to a cap, or (B) a partial price reset for remaining term but capped at a 10% downward adjustment to unit rates.

2) Guardrails we require:
   - Eligibility: applies only to base committed units (not burst/overage).
   - Cap: total commercial impact capped at 8% of the total committed value across the contract term (we can stretch to 10% with pricing committee sign‑off).
   - Invocation window: must be invoked within 120 days of the 90‑day lookback period ending.
   - Frequency: one invocation per contract term.

3) Operational/fulfillment note (Marcus): if customer chooses price reset, we should lock SKU mapping at invocation date to avoid churn in routing. Marcus — that implies a short ops checklist; please confirm feasibility.

Next steps: if Marcus confirms ops, I'll tidy language and send to Karthik/Kimberly for a quick legal/finance signoff. If legal flags material exposure, we'll escalate to price committee.

Ben
Head of Revenue Ops
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Agree with Ben's construct. Ops feasibility notes:
- If ClearSight opts for the price reset path, we'll record the SKU mapping and routing configuration as of the invocation date and continue serving under those pinned SKUs — no immediate rebalancing required.
- We will need a short-headcount window (~2–3 business days) to run a reconciliation job and lock capacity pools; this is purely a state/record operation and doesn't require provisioning new hardware.
- Risk: if invocation occurs late in the contract term (<6 months remaining), the economic benefit to the customer will be limited; suggest we include a minimum remaining-term threshold (>=6 months) for the reset option to be valid.

Marcus

Subject: Re: GPU price protection for reserved commit? — proposed safety‑net clause and next steps

Alex / Jordan — thanks for raising this. Attached is a proposed safety‑net clause and an overview of the mechanics (two remedy options, trigger definition, and guardrails). Summary of what we can offer (approved by Revenue Ops and Product Ops):

- Trigger: 90‑day trailing average market delta >25% vs. the Redwood GPU Index.
- Remedy (customer choice at invocation):
   1) One‑time invoice credit equal to 50% of the delta applied to upcoming invoices up to a cap, OR
   2) One‑time unit‑rate reset for remaining term capped at a 10% reduction to committed unit rates, subject to a minimum of 6 months remaining on the contract when invoked.
- Caps & frequency: single invocation per contract. Total commercial impact capped at 8% of total committed spend (we can consider up to 10% with Exec approval).
- Eligibility: applies to base committed capacity only.
- Process: invocation requires written notice, Redwood will validate against the Redwood GPU Index and publish the validation report within 10 business days. If customer elects the reset option, ops will pin SKU mapping as of the invocation date.

I've attached a redlined clause for your counsel to review and a DocuSign starter link if you'd like to proceed with these terms. If this looks okay, we can route the brief redline to your legal team and get this into the contract for signature.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/clearsight-deal-2987
Attachments: redline-safety-net-clause.docx; gpu-pricing-scenarios.xlsx

Please let me know if you want a short call to walk through the mechanics; otherwise, if counsel is happy, we'll aim to have an executed amendment by next week.
